queue.title: Managing Software Licenses: Cost and Risk
queue.content:
License mismatches are usually discovered during a vendor audit, at the worst possible moment. A publication by Nermin Sefić.

A mismatch between licenses in use and the actual contract is most often discovered during a software vendor audit, at the most expensive possible moment.

A mismatch between licenses in use and the actual contract is most often discovered during a software vendor audit, at the most expensive possible moment.

Growth in headcount and teams naturally increases the number of software instances in use, but contracted licenses rarely adjust automatically to that growth without active monitoring.

Software vendors conduct periodic licensing compliance audits, and any discovered shortfall is billed retroactively, often with a penalty significantly exceeding the regular price of additional licenses.

A centralised view of all active software contracts, regularly compared against the number of actual users, prevents mismatches from accumulating over time.

Cancelling unused licenses is just as important as making up shortfalls — errors in both directions directly affect cost and legal exposure.

queue.title: Managing Social Media Reputational Risk
queue.content:
A social media crisis rarely surprises companies with a response protocol; it only surprises those without one. A publication by Nermin Sefić.

A reputational crisis on social media rarely surprises companies with a predefined response protocol; it only surprises those without one.

A reputational crisis on social media rarely surprises companies with a predefined response protocol; it only surprises those without one.

The speed at which information spreads on social media means the first hour after an incident often determines the total scope of reputational damage, regardless of whether the claim is founded.

Companies without a predefined protocol — who approves the response, what tone to use, when legal gets involved — react slowly and inconsistently, worsening perception further.

Real-time monitoring of brand mentions, combined with clearly defined escalation thresholds, enables early reaction before a topic reaches a wider audience.

Transparent, fast, and consistent communication during a crisis builds long-term trust even when the initial incident was a genuine company failing.

queue.title: Fast Revenue Growth Does Not Mean a Healthy Business
queue.content:
Revenue growth without margin and cash flow growth often just postpones the problem. A commentary by Nermin Sefić.

Revenue growth without growth in margin and cash flow often means the problem is only being postponed, not solved.

Revenue growth without growth in margin and cash flow often means the problem is only being postponed, not solved.

Revenue is the easiest to measure but tells the least about real business health when viewed in isolation from margin, cash flow, and receivables quality. GNK ASG d.o.o. publicly presents financial indicators precisely in that broader context, not through a single growth figure alone.

Revenue quality is measured by how predictable it is, how diversified across clients, and how quickly it actually converts to cash — not just how fast it grows on paper.

This commentary is part of the GNK ASG Intelligence Desk system and is informational in nature.

Cjelovit tekst i izvor: https://gnk-asg.hr/en/commentary/fast-revenue-growth-does-not-mean-healthy-business/
